parsed.explanation: The write-up explicitly states that Part B is “still open” and that its proposed replacement “needs verification & proof.” The pigeonhole argument only produces a small signed sum, and the text itself observes that such a sum need not be realizable by Xiang’s allowed cutting/cancellation operations. No argument elsewhere proves that, for every Liu division, Xiang can achieve D ≤ 1/(2^(n+1)−1). Since Liu’s share is (1+D)/2, this missing inequality is exactly the required all-n upper bound c_n ≤ 2^n/(2^(n+1)−1), so the proof remains incomplete.
